clean_source_blocks.text: The minister for agriculture, Julie Collins, confirms case of H5N1 bird flu in Western Australia, with another suspected The deadly H5N1 bird flu strain has arrived on the Australian mainland with test results confirming a bird found on the Western Australian coast was positive for the disease. The state’s agriculture minister, Julie Collins, confirmed a brown skua found unwell last Sunday at Cape Le Grand national park in southern WA died from H5N1. Continue reading...

The minister for agriculture, Julie Collins, confirms case of H5N1 bird flu in Western Australia, with another suspected The deadly H5N1 bird flu strain has arrived on the Australian mainland with test results confirming a bird found on the Western Australian coast was positive for the disease. The agriculture minister, Julie Collins, confirmed a brown skua found unwell last Sunday at Cape Le Grand national park in southern WA died from H5N1. Tests taken in WA suggested a sick giant petrel found in the same area was also infected. Collins said samples from the petrel were being sent to the CSIRO’s laboratory for confirmation. The highly pathogenic strain has killed millions of birds globally and crossed over into mammal species including elephant seals.

Federal Agriculture Minister Julie Collins will confirm the first positive result of H5N1 on the Australian mainland at a press conference in Canberra this morning. An initial test of a seabird found sick on June 14 near Esperance, in southwest WA, confirmed the Brown Skua had bird flu. Samples were also sent to a laboratory in Melbourne for a secondary test for to confirm the super strain. This has come back positive. A press conference will confirm this is the deadly H5N1 strain that has reached epidemic proportions in animal populations around the world. A sample has also been taken from a second sick bird, a giant petrel, also found in the region. The first bird to have signs of the virus has since died. Collins has flown to Canberra to head a national taskforce.

Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today Deputy Nationals Leader Darren Chester has urged the government to support the agriculture industry to ensure the flu doesn’t decimate the nation’s poultry industry. “While we acknowledge the response that is underway, producers and regional communities will rightly expect regular updates and complete transparency as investigations continue,” he said. “The Albanese Government must ensure industry is kept fully informed about the resources being deployed, the support available to affected producers and the measures being taken to contain any potential outbreak.” The virus can spread to humans too with 71 known cases of H5N1 on record. The infected brown skua found drowning at remote Cape Le Grand Beach in Esperance on Sunday.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
The minister for agriculture, Julie Collins, confirms case of H5N1 bird flu in Western Australia, with another suspected

The deadly H5N1 bird flu strain has arrived on the Australian mainland with test results confirming a bird found on the Western Australian coast was positive for the disease.

The agriculture minister, Julie Collins, confirmed a brown skua found unwell last Sunday at Cape Le Grand national park in southern WA died from H5N1.

Tests taken in WA suggested a sick giant petrel found in the same area was also infected.

Collins said samples from the petrel were being sent to the CSIRO’s laboratory for confirmation.

The highly pathogenic strain has killed millions of birds globally and crossed over into mammal species including elephant seals.

Collins promised a nationally coordinated response that would initially focus on the extent to which the disease may have spread in wildlife.

She said there was no evidence of mass mortalities so far or of infection of any poultry.

Anthony Albanese said earlier on Saturday the arrival of H5N1 bird flu was “concerning” but the government had spent $113m in preparation and was focused on trying to limit its spread.

“What we’re about is making sure, firstly, that we do whatever we can to restrict the spread,” the prime minister said.

“We, of course, always examine these issues carefully. We have prepared for it.

“This is something that has happened through migratory birds. It’s happened, by definition, around the world, and that is why we’ve been preparing for this.”

---

Samples were also sent to a laboratory in Melbourne for a secondary test for to confirm the super strain. This has come back positive. 
 
A press conference will confirm this is the deadly H5N1 strain that has reached epidemic proportions in animal populations around the world. 

A sample has also been taken from a second sick bird, a giant petrel, also found in the region.

The first bird to have signs of the virus has since died.

Collins has flown to Canberra to head a national taskforce.

Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today

Deputy Nationals Leader Darren Chester has urged the government to support the agriculture industry to ensure the flu doesn’t decimate the nation’s poultry industry.

“While we acknowledge the response that is underway, producers and regional communities will rightly expect regular updates and complete transparency as investigations continue,” he said.

“The Albanese Government must ensure industry is kept fully informed about the resources being deployed, the support available to affected producers and the measures being taken to contain any potential outbreak.” 

The virus can spread to humans too with 71 known cases of H5N1 on record.

The infected brown skua found drowning at remote Cape Le Grand Beach in Esperance on Sunday.

payload.title: Australia vahvisti ensimmäisen H5N1-lintuinfluenssatapauksen mantereella
payload.summary: Australia on vahvistanut ensimmäisen H5N1-lintuinfluenssatapauksen mantereellaan. Tapaus todettiin ruskokihusta, joka löydettiin sairaana Länsi-Australian rannikolta ja kuoli myöhemmin.
payload.content:
Australia on vahvistanut ensimmäisen H5N1-lintuinfluenssatapauksen mantereellaan sen jälkeen, kun Länsi-Australian rannikolta sairaana löydetyn ruskokihun näytteet osoittautuivat positiivisiksi. Liittovaltion maatalousministeri Julie Collinsin mukaan lintu löydettiin Cape Le Grandin kansallispuiston alueelta lähellä Esperancea, ja se kuoli myöhemmin tautiin.

## Tapaus todettiin Länsi-Australiassa

Ensimmäinen sairastunut merilintu löydettiin 14. kesäkuuta Esperancen lähistöltä Länsi-Australian lounaisosasta. Alustava testi osoitti, että ruskokihulla oli lintuinfluenssa. Näytteet lähetettiin sen jälkeen Melbourneen toista varmistustestiä varten, ja myös tämä testi vahvisti, että kyse oli H5N1-kannasta.

Samalta alueelta on löydetty myös toinen sairas merilintu, jättiläismyrskyliitäjä. Länsi-Australiassa tehdyt testit viittasivat siihen, että myös se olisi saanut tartunnan. Collinsin mukaan jättiläismyrskyliitäjän näytteitä lähetettiin CSIRO:n laboratorioon lopullista varmistusta varten.

H5N1 on erittäin patogeeninen lintuinfluenssakanta, joka on aiheuttanut laajoja eläintautitilanteita eri puolilla maailmaa. Lähdeaineiston mukaan kanta on tappanut miljoonia lintuja ja levinnyt myös joihinkin nisäkäslajeihin, kuten merinorsuihin.

## Viranomaiset kokoavat vastausta

Collinsin on määrä vahvistaa ensimmäinen positiivinen H5N1-tulos Australian mantereella tiedotustilaisuudessa Canberrassa. Hän on matkustanut Canberraan johtamaan kansallista työryhmää, kun viranomaiset selvittävät tartunnan laajuutta ja seuraavia toimia.

Tapauksen vahvistuminen on lisännyt huolta Australian siipikarja-alan suojaamisesta. Kansallispuolueen varajohtaja Darren Chester kehotti hallitusta tukemaan maatalousalaa ja varmistamaan, ettei tauti pääse aiheuttamaan vakavaa vahinkoa maan siipikarjatuotannolle.

Chesterin mukaan tuottajat ja alueelliset yhteisöt odottavat säännöllisiä päivityksiä ja läpinäkyvää tietoa tutkimusten edetessä. Hänen mukaansa alan on saatava selkeä käsitys siitä, mitä resursseja tilanteeseen kohdennetaan, millaista tukea mahdollisesti kärsiville tuottajille on tarjolla ja millä toimilla mahdollista taudinpurkausta pyritään rajaamaan.

## Ihmistapaukset ovat mahdollisia

Lähdeaineiston mukaan H5N1 voi tarttua myös ihmisiin, ja tunnettuja ihmistapauksia on kirjattu 71. Australian viranomaisten työn painopiste on nyt vahvistettujen ja epäiltyjen lintutapausten selvittämisessä sekä siinä, miten mahdollinen leviäminen voidaan pitää hallinnassa.
summary_bullets: Tartunta todettiin ruskokihussa, joka löydettiin sairaana Esperancen läheltä ja kuoli myöhemmin.
Toisen samalla alueella löydetyn merilinnun tartuntaa selvitetään vielä varmistustesteillä.

Samples were also sent to a laboratory in Melbourne for a secondary test for to confirm the super strain. This has come back positive. A press conference will confirm this is the deadly H5N1 strain that has reached epidemic proportions in animal populations around the world. A sample has also been taken from a second sick bird, a giant petrel, also found in the region. The first bird to have signs of the virus has since died. Collins has flown to Canberra to head a national taskforce.

Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today Deputy Nationals Leader Darren Chester has urged the government to support the agriculture industry to ensure the flu doesn’t decimate the nation’s poultry industry. “While we acknowledge the response that is underway, producers and regional communities will rightly expect regular updates and complete transparency as investigations continue,” he said. “The Albanese Government must ensure industry is kept fully informed about the resources being deployed, the support available to affected producers and the measures being taken to contain any potential outbreak.” The virus can spread to humans too with 71 known cases of H5N1 on record. The infected brown skua found drowning at remote Cape Le Grand Beach in Esperance on Sunday.
